newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ousted Afghan leader Dostum arrives in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Afghan leader Dostum arrives in Turkey.

text.p: General Abdul Rashid Dostum, ousted from his fiefdom in northern Afghanistan by Islamic Taleban fighters, arrived on Sunday in the Turkish capital Ankara, said a spokesman for the Turkish foreign ministry.
"General Rashid Dostum arrived in Ankara this morning," the ministry spokesman said. He gave no other details.

Pictures made available to Reuters Television showed Dostum, his wife and family arriving in the Turkish capital with suitcases. He checked into an Ankara hotel after travelling from the airport in a limousine.

Dostum's northern capital of Mazar-i-Sharif on Sunday appeared to be under the control of rival ethnic Uzbek fighters who had until last week been part of an alliance opposing the purist Taleban movement, Reuters reporters on the scene said.
Turkey was widely reported to have supported the ethnic Uzbek leader Dostum, along with Uzbekistan. Turks and Uzbeks share common ethnic and linguistic links.
The advance by the Taleban ends an eight-month standoff between the Islamic movement and a fragile coalition linking Dostum with former Afghan government forces.
The coalition's defences fell apart when Dostum's key commander Malik defected to the Taleban last Monday, exposing the alliance's western flank.
